(i) a monitor is able to detect an attack if and only if the attack is not indistinguishable from a legitimate system behavior; (ii) the detection capability of a monitor depends on its observability, which is related to the number of sensors and their location in the system; (iii) the detection capability is not affected by the number of actuators; (iv) the attack identification capability is determined by the monitor’s controllability, and is independent of the number of sensors
